## Observation

During the df72 store repair on 2026-10-28, the local `tickets` branch had local-only commits while also trailing `origin/tickets` (related history, each side with unique commits). `rebar store fsck` reported:

```
DIVERGED: local 'tickets' branch has diverged from origin/tickets — no shared history / cannot fast-forward. The local store was built independently of the remote (e.g. init could not fetch the existing branch), so it hides remote tickets and its writes will never push. Recover: run `rebar fsck-recover`, or re-clone and re-init
```

## Defects

`_tracker_sync_status` in `src/rebar/_commands/fsck_tracker_health.py` uses one message for two different states:

1. No common ancestor (`git merge-base` fails). The text fits this case.
2. A common ancestor exists, but neither side contains the other. The text is false here: the histories are shared, the store was not "built independently", and re-cloning would discard the local-only commits, which may hold ticket events not yet on the remote.

Separately, the recovery advice names `rebar fsck-recover`, which is not a command. `rebar fsck-recover` fails with `invalid choice`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The related-but-diverged case reports its own message: local and remote share history, the counts of local-only and remote-only commits, and a non-destructive recovery path that preserves local-only commits.
- [ ] The no-common-ancestor case keeps a message that fits it.
- [ ] Neither message names a command that does not exist. A test checks that every rebar command named in the advice is a real subcommand.
- [ ] Tests cover both cases.
compiled_state.title: fsck DIVERGED message claims no shared history for a related divergence and names a nonexistent recovery command
